w.why: RE-RULED from 1066 by Ruling 15 (ANDON 2): 1066 is not a legal generator width - the Qwen VAE downsamples by 8, so 1066 encodes to 133 latent columns and decodes to 1064, breaking every twin<->silhouette pairing. 1072 is divisible by 16, is this subject's own Gate 0 frame (Ruling 6), and the fit is verified: at margin 1.204 the extra 6 px is slack, not distortion. HISTORICAL DERIVATION (kept because it was correct as geometry): widest projected width 0.9987 at yaw 0, height 0.9598, aspect 1.0405, 1024 * 1.0405 = 1066; broadside genuinely widest, bbox understates by 0.00%. The standing rule leaving this arc: derive the frame from the mesh, then round to the nearest generator-legal width.

views.why: Eight eye-level yaws. Kept at eight because the elevated cameras are where this subject's coverage is bought, not the eye-level count - see cameras below.

yaw-offset.why: MEASURED, and deliberately zero. The bow is the -x end (2,308 verts, beam 0.103 - a thin low bowsprit) and the stern is +x (12,748 verts, beam 0.170, carrying the spired turret), confirmed by eye on the clay renders where the turret sits image-right at yaw 0. So view 0 is the port broadside, view 2 is stern-on, view 6 is bow-on. Left at zero because the broadside is a ship's maximum-information view and rotating buys nothing measurable - and the camera is what would rotate, never the mesh (to_mesh() destroys authored vertex normals).

texpass_brush.py._the_block_was_NOT_CLEARED_and_this_is_t: Ruling 23 lifted it, and the lifecycle Ruling 22 ratified is why every key below carries a decision: removing the marker reverts these seven keys to UNDECIDED and --coverage fires. That firing is the procedure, not a defect - the ruling that clears a tool pays for the clearance by deciding its keys in the same commit. HISTORICAL TEXT: 'FORBIDDEN on the ship until this block carries ruled values - Ruling 14, standing law. The tool's --prompt defaults to the literal W3 identity string (Ruling 2's named accident class); the ship's brush prompts are _fixtures.brush_prompts, still REQUIRED NOT WRITTEN, and stroke cameras derive from the hole map after projection.'
texpass_brush.py._THE_FIVE_RECIPE_NUMBERS_BELOW_DO_NOT_RE: FINDING, reported in the derivation report and not silently absorbed. Generation is cloud-only, so a ship stroke runs through brush_cloud_step.py, which posts nothing local; texpass_brush.py posts to 127.0.0.1:8188 and will not run on this subject. brush_cloud_step.py BINDS NO PROFILE - it carries its own DEFAULTS = {seed 770700, steps 20, cfg 2.5, lora_w 0.75, cn_strength 1.0} and a hardcoded CLOUD_LORA, and takes prompt and negative from the prompts file. So of the seven keys here, prompt and negative reach the graph through _fixtures.brush_prompts, and the five numbers reach it through that tool's own constants. They AGREE today because Ruling 23 set them to exactly those values - by coincidence of value, not by construction. This is armT-halt2 Finding B's mechanism at a fourth site, and --coverage cannot see it because brush_cloud_step.py has no block in character.json either.

thin-extent.why: MEASURED on this mesh, by the same method the character's 0.030 came from - the smallest value that fills the thin structure solid, judged on the artifact. Three independent lines agree: (1) the extent DENSITY has its thin peak at 0.0015-0.0045, which at this render scale is 1.3-4 px, matching rigging diameters; (2) rendered thin-masks at 0.005 leave the rigging PATCHY and at 0.010 it is solid, because a rope crossing the ray obliquely presents more extent than its diameter; (3) the cross-view cost at 0.010 is 10.20% of visible area withheld on EVERY view, against 15.25% at the character's 0.030. NOT an antimode: the density falls steeply into a plateau rather than a valley, so this is a visual-solidity determination like W3's, not a discovered boundary. The cost curve is published in the report so it can be moved. Frame re-ruled 1066->1072 (Ruling 15): px scale shifts 0.56%, within this derivation's own slack - value unchanged.

The character path is untouched: no code default changed, so its cull output is unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by re-measurement.

production.why: The code default's 24-yaw sweep and both elevated pairs, PLUS the ship's adopted 0/180 @ 40. A superset, never a narrowing - the classification must cover cameras nobody has added yet, which is why my Task 2 draft was wrong to write the subject's ten cameras here.

cameras._stage_assignment_RULED: Ruling 13: the eye-level eight are STAGE 1 - the twin cameras. The elevated pair is STAGE 2 data - stroke-camera candidates (texpass_iter emit --el) plus cull-superset coverage - exactly as on the character, whose stage 1 is eye-level BY CONSTRUCTION (turn_render camera at mid.z; silhouette_masks and project_twins ray z hardcoded 0; E08's eight all-yaw). No route tool can render, mask or project an elevated twin; that capability would be a Step-0-class arm of its own (three tools, character byte-identity anchors), recorded as available and NOT opened. The spec's 'ten cameras' twins line was the advisor's slip, corrected in its Amendment 1.
cameras._measured_by_raycast_deck_coverage: The design note flagged 'decks need looking into' as a real design question. Made a number: upward-facing surface is identified by normal (normal_z > 0.5) and each candidate set scored by what fraction of that surface's AREA it first-hits. Area, not face count - a deck is a few large triangles and the rigging is thousands of tiny ones, so counting would have measured the rigging and called it deck.

eye_level.why: Eight yaws at elevation 0. On their own they reach only 30.17% of upward-facing area - a ship's decks are largely invisible from eye level, which is the measurement behind the design note's intuition.

elevated.why: MEASURED as a union, not per-elevation. Adding this bow/stern pair at 40 degrees takes deck coverage 30.17% -> 49.58%, the largest gain available from two cameras. Three findings decided it: (a) the pair is worth +19.41 points, far more than the character's elevated pair bought there; (b) bow/stern BEATS beam - the same pair at 90/270 reaches only 41.93%, because looking along the ship's length sees down the decks while looking across the beam is blocked by hull sides and sails; (c) elevation is nearly free between 30 and 55 (49.21 / 49.58 / 49.15) so 40 is chosen as the measured peak rather than by inheriting the character's 55.

_considered_and_not_adopted.quad at 40 (adds 90/270): 53.21% deck, +3.63 over the pair, for two more cameras and two more brush strokes. Available if E04 wants it; the marginal camera buys a fifth of what the first pair did.
_considered_and_not_adopted.single top-down (0 @ 90): 42.97% deck for ONE camera - the most efficient single addition measured, but it caps lower than the pair and sees only 12.85% of total surface.
_considered_and_not_adopted.character's 0/180 @ 55: 49.15% - within 0.43 points of the adopted pair. The character value is not WRONG here, it is simply not derived; 40 is.

cameras._ceiling_worth_knowing: Deck coverage plateaus near 53% even at twelve cameras. Roughly half of this subject's upward-facing surface is not reachable from any exterior camera at these angles - it is under sails, yards and tops. That is a fact about the subject, and it means dilation and the brush will serve a large share of the deck however the camera set is chosen.

backdrop.why: DERIVED (Task 4b), not inherited. The key is max-channel |pixel - backdrop| > 0.06 and the backdrop is the only free operand, so it is chosen to maximise the minimum distance to every declared material, weighted toward the thin elements that antialias toward it. White scores raw-min 0.4275 (nearest: G10 pale deck) and thin-min 0.7176, against W3's inherited mid grey at raw-min 0.1725 and thin-min 0.2588 - a 2.5x improvement on the quantity that killed the blade. The dark thin elements this is chosen for sit furthest of all: G3 tarred strakes 0.8902, G9 rigging 0.8510, G8 cannon 0.8275.
backdrop._the_metric_optimum_was_rejected_and_why: Unconstrained, the metric picks saturated blue rgb(0,0,245) at weighted-min 0.3882 - it beats white by 8%, and it is disqualified twice over: the fixture requires avoiding G11's declared sea-blue, and a saturated backdrop bleeds into a diffusion image. The pre-registered tension (a metric-optimal backdrop being unusably coloured) dissolved rather than resolved: the practical answer is a plain neutral word.
backdrop._weakest_link_named: The material colours are ESTIMATES from the fixture's words. Re-run e04_backdrop.py against measured colours once the styled target pair exists; if the pair disagrees, the pair wins.

THE HONEST HEADLINE IS THAT THE ORDER IS NEARLY INERT ON THIS SUBJECT: stage 1 painted all eight yaws, so every candidate camera opens between 64% and 88% anchored and none is near the character's 95%-hole disaster case.
